t: Cold-launch splash presentation
pre: App fully closed before launch.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1.
2. Observe the splash presentation.
exp:
1. Splash opens without blank/corrupt content.
2. GlucoRx CGMx™ 1 product identity is displayed without missing, substituted, distorted or clipped app-owned content.

t: Splash transition to Welcome
pre: App fully closed before launch.
proc: 1. Launch CGMx 1 and observe the splash through transition to the next screen.
exp: 1. Splash transitions to the Welcome screen with no hang, crash, blank state or repeated splash loop.

t: Welcome screen content
pre: The Welcome screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Inspect the complete Welcome screen from top to bottom.
2. Compare the product image, text, icons, privacy message and actions with the approved iOS Welcome reference.
exp:
1. The screen shows the CGMx 1 product image and the heading See your glucose, clearly.
2. The supporting text reads: Real-time readings, smart alerts, and sharing that helps you stay in range — every day.
3. The three benefits read: Live readings every few minutes; Alerts you can act on — even on Silent; Share with the people who matter. Each benefit has its corresponding icon.
4. The screen shows Your data is private and secure. with the Learn more link.
5. Get started and Sign in are visible and available. No content is missing, duplicated, clipped, overlapping or corrupted.
ev: Full Welcome screenshot compared with IMG_6417.PNG; execution record.

t: Welcome privacy information link
pre: The Welcome screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Select Learn more beside Your data is private and secure.
2. Observe the destination.
3. Return to the app using the available back or close action.
exp:
1. Learn more responds once.
2. The intended privacy or data-security information opens without a blank page, unrelated destination or error.
3. Returning restores the Welcome screen without starting registration or authentication.
ev: Learn more destination and returned Welcome screen; execution record.

t: Android Back from Welcome
pre: Android only. The Welcome screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Press the Android system Back control once.
2. Open CGMx 1 again.
exp:
1. CGMx 1 closes or moves to the background without opening an earlier app screen or starting an account action.
2. CGMx 1 returns to a usable Welcome screen without a blank screen, crash or duplicate navigation.
ev: Android Back behavior and reopened Welcome screen; execution record.

t: Get started navigation
pre: The Welcome screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc: 1. Select Get started once.
exp: 1. The native Create Account screen opens once without an intermediate Sign In screen, blank state, crash or duplicate destination.
ev: Welcome and native Create Account screens; execution record.

t: Sign in navigation
pre: The Welcome screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc: 1. Select Sign in once.
exp: 1. The native Sign In screen opens once without a blank state, crash, unrelated destination or duplicate navigation.
ev: Welcome and native Sign In screens; execution record.

t: Welcome back screen content
pre: The user is signed out and the native Welcome back screen is displayed.
proc:
1. Inspect the image, CGMx 1 logo, heading and introduction at the top of the screen.
2. Inspect the Sign in action and the Forgot your password? link.
3. Inspect the data-protection card.
4. Inspect the Create an account link and the app version at the bottom of the screen.
5. Compare the whole screen with the approved iOS reference.
exp:
1. The lifestyle image, CGMx 1 logo, Welcome back heading and Sign in to pick up where you left off. are shown.
2. Sign in and Forgot your password? are shown.
3. The card reads Your health data is protected and Your information is encrypted in transit and at rest.
4. New to Modus? Create an account and the app version are shown. The reference version is Version 1.0.4 (202609301).
5. No content is missing, duplicated, clipped, overlapping or corrupted.
ev: Full screen compared with the approved iOS reference; displayed version; execution record.

t: Launch hosted GlucoRx sign-in
pre: The user is signed out, internet is available and the native Welcome back screen is displayed.
proc: 1. Select Sign in once.
exp: 1. The hosted GlucoRx Sign in page opens in the in-app browser with Email and Password fields, without a blank page, crash or native credential form.
ev: Welcome back screen before the action; hosted Sign in page; execution record.

t: Navigate between Welcome back and Create your account screens
pre: The user is signed out and the native Welcome back screen is displayed.
proc:
1. Select Create an account.
2. Select Sign in in Already have an account? Sign in.
exp:
1. The native Create your account screen opens with its content displayed.
2. The Welcome back screen opens again with its content restored.
ev: Create your account and Welcome back screenshots or recording; execution record.

t: Leave and return to Native Sign In (Android)
pre: User is logged out. Android device only.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1.
2. Press the Android Back button/gesture to leave Native Sign In.
3. Reopen CGMx 1.
exp:
1. Native Sign In screen opens.
2. Back returns to the previous unauthenticated state without submitting credentials.
3. Native Sign In screen opens again, with no duplicate screen or broken navigation.
ev: Screenshot/recording of departure destination and reopened Native Sign In; execution record

t: Background and resume CGMx 1 from Native Sign In (iOS)
pre: User is logged out. iOS device only.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1.
2. Swipe up to the Home Screen (or open the App Switcher) to background CGMx 1.
3. Bring CGMx 1 back to the foreground.
exp:
1. Native Sign In screen opens.
2. CGMx 1 moves to the background without submitting credentials or closing the app.
3. CGMx 1 resumes on the same Native Sign In screen, with no corrupted state.
ev: Screenshot/recording of departure destination and reopened Native Sign In; execution record

t: Hosted sign-in with no internet and recovery
pre: The user is signed out, the native Welcome back screen is displayed and internet is available.
proc:
1. Turn Airplane mode on and make sure Wi-Fi is off.
2. Select Sign in on the Welcome back screen.
3. Select the X (close) button at the top left of the in-app browser.
4. Turn Airplane mode off and wait until Wi-Fi or mobile data is connected.
5. Select Sign in again.
exp:
1. The device has no internet connection.
2. Sign-in does not complete. The in-app browser shows a loading or connection error; record the exact text shown.
3. The in-app browser closes and the Welcome back screen is shown. The user is still signed out.
4. The device is connected and the Welcome back screen is still shown.
5. The hosted GlucoRx Sign in page opens with Email and Password fields, without a blank page, crash or duplicate page.
ev: Offline error screenshot with the exact text; Welcome back screen after closing; hosted Sign in page after recovery; execution record.

sec: Batch 5 - Native Create Account and Consent
t: Create your account screen content
pre: The native Create your account screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Inspect the complete screen from top to bottom.
2. Compare the image, text, controls and version with the approved iOS reference.
exp:
1. The screen shows the lifestyle image, CGMx 1 logo and Create your account heading.
2. The explanation states: It takes about a minute. You'll set your email and password on the secure GlucoRx page, then confirm your email address.
3. Separate Terms of Service and Privacy Policy consent controls and their Read links are shown.
4. Create account is disabled and Please accept both to continue. is shown while both controls are unchecked.
5. The security card reads Your health data is protected and Your information is encrypted in transit and at rest.
6. Already have an account? Sign in and the app version are visible. For IMG_6418.PNG the displayed reference is Version 1.0.4 (202609301). No content is missing, duplicated, clipped, overlapping or corrupted.
ev: Full screen compared with IMG_6418.PNG; displayed version; execution record.

sec: Batch 5 - Native Create Account and Consent
t: Terms and Privacy consent presentation
pre: The native Create your account screen is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Inspect both consent controls before selecting either one.
2. Inspect the legal text and link associated with each control.
exp:
1. Two separate controls are shown and both are unchecked by default.
2. The first control is associated with I agree to the Terms of Service and Read Terms of Service.
3. The second control is associated with I have read and accept the Privacy Policy and Read Privacy Policy.
4. No consent is preselected or implied by opening the screen.
ev: Initial unchecked consent controls and associated text; execution record.

sec: Batch 5 - Native Create Account and Consent
t: Create account consent gating
pre: The native Create your account screen is displayed with both consent controls unchecked.
proc:
1. Confirm Create account is unavailable and the helper message is displayed.
2. Select only the Terms of Service consent.
3. Select the Privacy Policy consent as well.
4. Deselect either consent.
exp:
1. Create account is disabled and Please accept both to continue. is shown.
2. Create account remains disabled while only one consent is selected.
3. Create account becomes enabled when both consents are selected.
4. Deselecting either consent disables Create account again. No registration starts during these checks.
ev: Zero, one, two and deselected consent states; execution record.

sec: Batch 5 - Native Create Account and Consent
t: Terms of Service and Privacy Policy links
pre: The native Create your account screen is displayed and internet is available.
proc:
1. Select Read Terms of Service.
2. Return to Create your account.
3. Select Read Privacy Policy.
4. Return to Create your account.
exp:
1. The GlucoRx Terms of Service resource opens without an error.
2. Returning restores Create your account; neither consent is selected automatically and registration does not start.
3. The GlucoRx Privacy Policy resource opens without an error.
4. Returning again restores Create your account without changing consent or account state.
ev: Terms resource, Privacy resource and returned consent states; execution record.

sec: Batch 5 - Native Create Account and Consent
t: Open hosted registration after consent
pre: The native Create your account screen is displayed, both consent controls are selected and internet is available.
proc:
1. Select Create account once.
2. Read the iOS sign-in prompt.
3. Select Continue.
4. Observe the hosted page.
exp:
1. Create account responds once and changes to a disabled Opening secure page... state with a progress indicator.
2. iOS shows “Modus” Wants to Use “keycloak.dev.platform.glucorx.co.uk” to Sign In, with the text This allows the app and website to share information about you. and Cancel and Continue buttons.
3. After Continue, the hosted GlucoRx Create your account page opens in the in-app browser with Email, Password, Confirm password, Given name(s), Family name(s) and Region. No duplicate page opens.
4. No account is created and the user is not signed in.
ev: Opening secure page... state, iOS prompt, hosted registration page; execution record.

t: Hosted Sign In page content
pre: The user is signed out, internet is available, and the native Sign In screen is displayed.
proc:
1. Select Sign in on the native Sign In screen and wait for the hosted page to open.
2. Inspect the hosted page branding, heading, instructions and credential fields without entering data.
3. Inspect the actions and footer shown below the credential fields.
4. Open the language selector, inspect all available languages, then close it without changing the language.
exp:
1. The hosted GlucoRx Sign In page opens once without a blank page, error or unrelated destination.
2. The page shows GlucoRx branding, the Sign in heading and Welcome back. Use your GlucoRx account to continue. Email and Password are marked required; Email shows you@example.com; Password has a visibility control; and Forgot password? is available.
3. Sign in, New to GlucoRx? Create an account, © 2026 GlucoRx Ltd and the language control are visible and readable, with no missing, duplicated, clipped or corrupted content.
4. The language selector offers English (UK), English (US), Cymraeg, العربية and Español. Closing it without a selection leaves the page language unchanged.
ev: Native Sign In screen, complete Hosted Sign In page and expanded language list; execution record.

t: Sign In email input handling
pre: Hosted Sign In is open. A non-sensitive password is available.
proc:
1. Enter a valid-format test email, then clear it.
2. Enter malformed email text and the non-sensitive password.
3. Select Sign in once.
exp:
1. Email accepts the valid-format value and clears normally.
2. The malformed value remains exactly as entered; the page does not show a separate email-format message.
3. Sign-in is rejected with Invalid username or password. and the user remains signed out.
ev: Valid, cleared and malformed Email states; generic rejection; execution record.

t: Sign In password required handling
pre: Hosted Sign In is open. A non-sensitive test email is available.
proc:
1. Enter the test email and leave Password empty.
2. Select Sign in once.
3. Enter a non-sensitive password.
exp:
1. Email retains the entered value and Password remains empty.
2. Sign-in is rejected with Invalid username or password. and the user remains signed out.
3. Password accepts the value and masks it by default.
ev: Empty-password rejection and masked Password state; execution record.

t: Password visibility control
pre: Hosted Sign In is open. A non-sensitive password is available.
proc:
1. Enter the password.
2. Select Show password.
3. Select the visibility control again.
exp:
1. Password is masked by default.
2. The existing value becomes visible without changing or submitting it.
3. The same value becomes masked again.
ev: Masked, visible and re-masked Password states; execution record.

t: Successful hosted Sign In - local onboarding already completed
pre: User is logged out; valid verified test account and correct password are available; internet is available. The application local onboarding-complete state already exists on the device.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1, then from Native Sign In tap Sign in.
2. Enter the valid account email and correct password.
3. Tap Sign In.
exp:
1. Hosted Sign In page opens.
2. Credentials are entered normally.
3. Authentication succeeds, control returns to the app, and the user proceeds directly to the applicable sensor-setup state (existing local onboarding-complete state respected) rather than restarting onboarding.

t: Successful hosted Sign In - fresh/reinstalled local state
pre: User is logged out; valid verified test account and correct password are available; internet is available. App local onboarding state has been reset by a fresh install/reinstall.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1, then from Native Sign In tap Sign in.
2. Enter the valid account email and correct password.
3. Tap Sign In.
exp:
1. Hosted Sign In page opens.
2. Credentials are entered normally.
3. Authentication succeeds, control returns to the app, and fresh local onboarding starts (on iOS, Apple Health may be the first platform-specific screen; on Android, onboarding starts with the Bluetooth permission screen — the subsequent shared onboarding flow remains valid).

t: Reject an incorrect password
pre: Hosted Sign In is open. QA_ACTIVE_01 is available.
proc:
1. Enter the QA_ACTIVE_01 email and an incorrect password.
2. Select Sign in once.
3. Replace the password with the correct QA_ACTIVE_01 password and select Sign in once.
exp:
1. Email is retained and Password is masked.
2. Keycloak shows Invalid username or password. and the user remains signed out.
3. Corrected credentials authenticate successfully without restarting the app.
ev: Incorrect-password response and successful retry; execution record.

t: Unverified account login and activation-email resend
pre: User is logged out; internet is available. Requires a backend-provisioned test account (PRE-EXECUTION RESOURCE REQUIRED if not available) whose email activation is incomplete, its correct password, and an inbox accessible to the tester. Record the account identifier in the execution record.
proc:
1. Launch CGMx 1, then from Native Sign In tap Sign in.
2. Enter the unverified account email and correct password, then tap Sign In.
3. Confirm a re-send verification action is available and select it once.
4. Open the registered test inbox and confirm that a new activation/verification email is received. Do not use the link during this case.
exp:
1. Hosted Sign In page opens.
2. The unverified account does not enter the authenticated application; the hosted flow shows that email verification/activation is required.
3. Selecting re-send causes a new activation/verification email to be sent to the registered test address.
4. The account remains unverified until a valid activation link is completed, and the new email arrives at the registered inbox.
ev: Activation-required screen; re-send action/result; received activation email showing recipient and language; execution record

t: Cancel hosted Sign In before authentication
pre: Duplicate coverage identified during execution review.
proc: Removed from Batch 6 execution. Equivalent hosted-flow cancellation/return behavior is already covered by earlier executed sign-in navigation/return verification.
exp: No duplicate execution required. Existing earlier evidence remains authoritative for this behavior.
ev: Covered by earlier executed sign-in navigation/return evidence

pre: Duplicate coverage identified during execution review.
proc: Removed from Batch 6 execution because offline SSO initiation/recovery was already executed in the earlier Native Sign In batch.
exp: No duplicate execution required. Existing earlier offline SSO evidence remains authoritative; Quality/RA may restore this case only if a distinct hosted-submit-offline requirement is confirmed.
ev: Covered by earlier offline SSO execution evidence

t: Repeated Sign In tap does not create duplicate authentication flow
pre: The user is unauthenticated, internet is available, and Hosted Sign In is displayed. The QA_ACTIVE_01 email and password are available in the QA Workbook, Test Data row TD-01.2.
proc:
1. Enter the QA_ACTIVE_01 email in Email.
2. Enter the QA_ACTIVE_01 password from the QA Workbook, Test Data row TD-01.2.
3. Select Sign in twice rapidly.
exp:
1. The email is displayed in Email.
2. The password is masked.
3. One sign-in completes and CGMx 1 shows one destination screen; no duplicate browser page, stacked app screen, error or corrupted authentication state appears.
ev: Screen recording of the repeated sign-in action and resulting destination; execution record.

t: Authentication failure does not reveal account existence
pre: Hosted Sign In is open. QA_ACTIVE_01 and an unregistered test email are available.
proc:
1. Submit the QA_ACTIVE_01 email with an incorrect password and capture the response.
2. Submit the unregistered email with the same incorrect password and capture the response.
3. Compare both responses.
exp:
1. The registered-email attempt fails with Invalid username or password.
2. The unregistered-email attempt fails with the same Invalid username or password. response.
3. Neither response reveals whether the email is registered.
ev: Both generic authentication responses; execution record.

t: Restore server-held account data at the 90-day boundary after login
pre: Req: DI-825 / DO-916. Non-production QA only. QA-HISTORY-01 is active and verified, its password is held outside the protocol, and the tester is logged out. The controlled fixture contains readings intended to be 91, 90 and 89 days old at execution. The recorded reference values are 98, 100 and 102 mg/dL respectively.
proc:
1. Check the fixture ages immediately before execution. If necessary, refresh the three controlled readings so they are 91, exactly 90 and 89 days old, then record their timestamps and values.
2. Remove CGMx 1 or clear its local data, reinstall or relaunch it as applicable, and confirm the user is logged out.
3. Sign in with QA-HISTORY-01 through the normal hosted sign-in flow.
4. Complete the normal post-sign-in flow until Home is displayed without manually re-entering historical readings.
5. Open the Home/Reports historical view that includes the boundary dates and check the controlled readings.
exp:
1. The recorded fixture contains one reading more than 90 days old, one exactly 90 days old and one less than 90 days old at the execution time.
2. CGMx 1 starts in a fresh, logged-out state with no locally retained history.
3. Sign-in succeeds and the account's server-held data is restored without data from another account.
4. Home is displayed without the tester manually recreating the historical readings.
5. The exactly-90-day and less-than-90-day readings are available in the supported historical view; the more-than-90-day reading is excluded.
ev: Recorded 91/90/89-day fixture timestamps and values; fresh-state evidence; restored Home/Reports boundary view; execution record.

t: Hosted Sign In languages
pre: Hosted Sign In is open.
proc:
1. Select English (UK), English (US), Cymraeg, العربية and Español one at a time.
2. In each language inspect the heading, Email, Password, password visibility action, Forgot password?, Sign in and Create an account.
3. Submit non-sensitive invalid credentials once in each language.
exp:
1. Every listed language can be selected.
2. The Sign In labels and actions use the selected language and remain readable.
3. The generic authentication rejection uses the selected language and the user remains signed out.
ev: Hosted Sign In and one rejection state for each language; execution record.

t: Apply account regional configuration after sign in
pre: Req: DI-285 / DO-673. Non-production QA only. The user is logged out. Test Data provides two active, verified regional accounts with completed onboarding and different controlled region, glucose-unit and language mappings. Their passwords are held outside the protocol and the expected mapping for each account is recorded in Test Data.
proc:
1. Sign in using Account A.
2. Open Settings > User Profile.
3. Open Home.
4. Sign out using Settings > Account Security > Logout.
5. Sign in using Account B.
6. Open Settings > User Profile.
7. Open Home.
8. Open Settings > Language.
exp:
1. Account A signs in successfully.
2. Country/region matches Account A's controlled mapping.
3. Home glucose values use Account A's controlled glucose unit.
4. The user becomes unauthenticated.
5. Account B signs in successfully.
6. Country/region matches Account B and does not retain Account A's value.
7. Home glucose values use Account B's controlled unit and do not retain Account A's unit.
8. The language or fallback matches Account B where it is exposed by the app. Internal regional server routing is outside this manual case.
ev: Account A and Account B User Profile screenshots; Account A and Account B Home glucose-unit screenshots; Settings > Language screenshot where applicable; execution record.

t: Re-present incomplete onboarding after subsequent login
pre: The user is unauthenticated, internet is available, and Hosted Sign In is displayed. At least one unused, never-onboarded account is available in the onboarding pool.
proc:
1. Select the next unused onboarding-pool account, record its alias, and sign in using its credentials from the QA Workbook, Test Data row TD-13.3 or TD-13.4.
2. Complete the first onboarding screen and select Continue.
3. On the next onboarding screen, remove CGMx 1 using the TD-59.1 reset method, reinstall it and launch it.
4. Open the hosted sign-in flow and sign in again with the same account.
exp:
1. The selected alias is recorded, sign-in succeeds and the first onboarding screen is shown; its title is recorded.
2. The next onboarding screen is shown.
3. CGMx 1 opens on the Welcome screen in an unauthenticated state.
4. Sign-in succeeds and onboarding starts again from the first screen recorded in Step 1; Home is not shown until onboarding is completed.
ev: Recorded account alias; first onboarding screen before and after reinstall; execution record.

t: Hosted registration page content
pre: Hosted Registration is displayed and the user is signed out.
proc:
1. Inspect the page from the GlucoRx logo down to the Region field.
2. Inspect the notice below Region, Create an account, Back to sign in and the language selector.
3. Open the Region list, then close it without making a selection.
4. Open the language list, then close it without making a selection.
exp:
1. The page shows Create your account, the required-fields note, Email, Password, Confirm password, Given name(s), Family name(s), Region and two password-visibility controls. Email, Password, Confirm password, Given name(s) and Region are marked required. Family name(s) is not marked required.
2. The notice reads: This sets where your health data is stored. It can't be changed later, so choose carefully. Create an account is disabled and cannot be selected, even though it is shown in blue. It remains unavailable until every required field is complete and valid. Back to sign in and the language selector are shown.
3. Region offers United Kingdom and United States and stays empty when closed without a selection.
4. The language selector offers English (UK), English (US), Cymraeg, العربية and Español and the page language is unchanged when it is closed without a selection.
ev: Full Hosted Registration page; Region and language lists; execution record.

t: Given name required-field validation
pre: Hosted Registration is open.
proc:
1. Leave Given name(s) empty and complete Email, Password, Confirm password and Region with valid test data.
2. Enter a value in Given name(s).
3. Clear Given name(s) again.
exp:
1. Create an account remains unavailable while Given name(s) is empty. No Please specify this field. message is shown.
2. Given name(s) accepts and retains the value, and Create an account becomes available.
3. Create an account becomes unavailable again once Given name(s) is empty.
ev: Given name input and required-field validation; execution record.

t: Family name is optional
pre: Hosted Registration is open.
proc:
1. Complete Email, Password, Confirm password, Given name(s) and Region with valid test data. Leave Family name(s) empty.
2. Enter a value in Family name(s), then clear it.
3. Do not create the account.
exp:
1. Create an account becomes available with Family name(s) empty. No required-field message is shown for Family name(s).
2. Family name(s) accepts and retains the value, and Create an account stays available when the field is entered or cleared.
3. No account is created.
ev: Optional Family name state and enabled Create an account action; execution record.

t: Email format validation
pre: Hosted Registration is open.
proc:
1. Complete Password, Confirm password, Given name(s) and Region with valid test data.
2. Enter malformed text in Email.
3. Replace it with a valid-format test email. Do not create the account.
exp:
1. Create an account remains unavailable while Email is empty.
2. Keycloak shows Invalid email address. and Create an account remains unavailable.
3. The message is removed and Create an account becomes available.
ev: Valid and malformed Email states; validation message; execution record.

t: Password format validation
pre: Hosted Registration is open. Valid values for every other required field are available.
proc:
1. Use valid details in Email, Given name(s) and Region.
2. Enter matching passwords shorter than 12 characters that contain a number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character.
3. Enter matching passwords of at least 12 characters with no number.
4. Repeat with no lowercase letter, then no uppercase letter, then no special character.
5. Enter matching passwords of at least 12 characters containing a number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character. Do not create the account.
exp:
1. Create an account remains unavailable until a password is entered.
2. Keycloak shows Invalid password: minimum length 12.
3. Keycloak shows Invalid password: must contain at least 1 numerical digits.
4. Keycloak shows the matching message for each missing type: must contain at least 1 lower case characters; must contain at least 1 upper case characters; must contain at least 1 special characters.
5. No password-format message is shown and Create an account becomes available. Create an account stays unavailable in steps 2 to 4.
ev: Password-format messages and valid-password state; execution record.

t: Password confirmation validation
pre: Hosted Registration is open. Valid values for every other required field are available.
proc:
1. Use valid details in Email, Given name(s) and Region.
2. Enter a valid-format password in Password.
3. Enter a different valid-format password in Confirm password.
4. Change Confirm password to match Password. Do not create the account.
exp:
1. Password remains masked by default.
2. Create an account remains unavailable until Confirm password is entered.
3. Keycloak shows Password confirmation doesn't match. and Create an account remains unavailable.
4. The message is removed and Create an account becomes available.

t: Reject registration with an existing email
pre: Hosted Registration is open. QA_ACTIVE_01 is available.
proc:
1. Enter the QA_ACTIVE_01 email.
2. Enter valid matching passwords, Given name(s) and Region. Family name(s) may be left empty.
3. Select Create an account once.
exp:
1. The form accepts the entered values.
2. The request is submitted once.
3. Keycloak rejects the duplicate registration, does not create another account or authenticated session, and leaves a recoverable registration or sign-in path.
ev: Completed form, duplicate-account response and recoverable state; execution record.

t: Required registration fields
pre: Hosted Registration is displayed and valid test values are available.
proc:
1. Inspect Create an account on the empty form.
2. Complete Email, Password, Confirm password, Given name(s) and Region with valid values.
3. Clear Email, then restore it.
4. Clear Password, then restore it.
5. Clear Confirm password, then restore it.
6. Clear Given name(s), then restore it.
7. Clear Region, then restore it.
8. Enter a value in Family name(s), then clear it. Do not create the account.
exp:
1. Create an account is disabled and cannot be selected, even though it is shown in blue. No Please specify this field. message is shown on the empty form.
2. Create an account becomes available only after all five required fields contain acceptable values.
3. Create an account is unavailable while Email is empty and available again when Email is restored.
4. Create an account is unavailable while Password is empty and available again when Password is restored.
5. Create an account is unavailable while Confirm password is empty and available again when it is restored.
6. Create an account is unavailable while Given name(s) is empty and available again when it is restored.
7. Create an account is unavailable while Region is empty and available again when it is restored.
8. Create an account stays available whether Family name(s) contains a value or is empty.
ev: Empty-form action state, each cleared-field state and the completed valid form; execution record.

t: Create a new account
pre: Hosted Registration is open. Fresh email A and its inbox are available.
proc:
1. Enter Fresh email A, valid matching passwords, Given name(s) and Region. Family name(s) is optional.
2. Select Create an account once.
exp:
1. Create an account becomes available when all required values are valid.
2. The registration is submitted once and the email-verification state opens for Fresh email A without an unexpected error.
ev: Completed registration form and email-verification state; execution record.

t: Email verification page content
pre: VP-APP-HOSTED-REG-009 has created Fresh email A and the verification page is open.
proc: 1. Inspect the verification page from top to bottom.
exp: 1. The page identifies Fresh email A, explains that verification is required and provides the available resend or recovery action.

t: Receive the verification email
pre: Fresh email A has been registered and its inbox is available.
proc:
1. Open the newest verification email for Fresh email A.
2. Record the received time and stated link-validity period.
exp:
1. The verification email is addressed to Fresh email A, identifies the GlucoRx service and contains a verification link.
2. The email states the link-validity period.
ev: Verification email and recorded timing; execution record.

t: Verify an account with a valid link
pre: The newest verification email for Fresh email A is open and its link is still valid.
proc:
1. Open the verification link.
2. Complete the confirmation action shown on the hosted page.
exp:
1. The link opens the verification flow for Fresh email A.
2. Verification completes and the account is no longer unverified.
ev: Verification confirmation and completed state; execution record.

t: Reject an expired verification link
pre: Fresh email B is registered but unverified. Its verification email time and validity period are recorded.
proc:
1. Wait until the stated validity period has passed.
2. Open the expired verification link.
exp:
1. The execution record proves the link was opened after its stated validity period.
2. Verification does not complete, an expired-link message is shown and Fresh email B remains unverified.
ev: Email timing and expired-link response; execution record.

t: Resend verification after expiry
pre: Fresh email B remains unverified and its earlier verification link has expired.
proc:
1. Select the resend-verification action.
2. Open the newest email for Fresh email B.
3. Open its link within the stated validity period and complete confirmation.
exp:
1. A new verification email is sent to Fresh email B.
2. The new email contains a new verification link.
3. The new link completes verification for Fresh email B.
ev: Resend result, new email and completed verification; execution record.

t: Return to hosted sign in
pre: Hosted Registration is open and no field has been changed.
proc: 1. Select Back to sign in.
exp: 1. Hosted Sign In opens. No registration is submitted and the user remains signed out.
ev: Hosted Sign In page; execution record.

t: Close hosted registration
pre: Hosted Registration is open and the user is signed out.
proc: 1. Select the X (close) button at the top left of the hosted page.
exp: 1. The hosted view closes without creating an account, and the native Create Account screen returns in a usable signed-out state.
ev: Native Create Account screen after closing; execution record.

t: Hosted registration languages
pre: Hosted Registration is open.
proc:
1. In the hosted language selector, select English (UK), English (US), Cymraeg, العربية and Español one at a time.
2. For each language, inspect the heading, required-fields note, field labels, Region notice, Create an account and Back to sign in.
3. Trigger one required-field message in each language without creating an account.
exp:
1. Every listed language can be selected directly on the hosted page.
2. Registration labels, actions and the Region notice use the selected language and remain readable.
3. The required-field message uses the selected language. Changing language does not submit registration.
ev: Hosted form and one validation state for each language; execution record.

t: Select and retain the registration region
pre: Hosted Registration is open. QA_REG_REGION_01 and its inbox are available.
proc:
1. Open Region and verify that United Kingdom and United States are available.
2. Select the region assigned to QA_REG_REGION_01 and read the notice below Region.
3. Complete the required fields, create the account, verify its email and sign in.
4. Open Settings > User Profile and inspect the account region.
exp:
1. Region provides United Kingdom and United States.
2. The notice reads: This sets where your health data is stored. It can't be changed later, so choose carefully.
3. Registration and verification retain the selected region.
4. User Profile shows the same region and provides no control that changes it.
ev: Region options and notice, selected value, verification and User Profile region; execution record.

t: Apply glucose unit from the registration region
pre: Fresh UK-region and US-region emails are available. The expected unit for each region is recorded in Test Data.
proc:
1. Register and verify one account with United Kingdom selected, then sign in and open Profile Setup.
2. Record the Country and Glucose unit.
3. Repeat with a fresh account and United States selected.
4. Inspect whether either account can change its unit to conflict with its registered region.
exp:
1. The hosted registration form uses Region and does not show a separate glucose-unit field.
2. Each account's Profile Setup shows the Country and unit defined for its registered region in Test Data.
3. The user cannot create a Country/Glucose unit mismatch after registration.
ev: Both registration regions and both Profile Setup unit results; execution record.

t: Registration language and region mismatch warning
pre: Test Data identifies a hosted language, an incompatible registration region and the expected correction and continue actions.
proc:
1. Select the Test Data language in the hosted language selector.
2. Select the incompatible Region and complete the other required fields.
3. Select Create an account and use the correction action on the mismatch warning.
4. Repeat the mismatch and use the continue action.
exp:
1. The form uses the selected language and region.
2. Before registration completes, a warning explains that signed-in content is unavailable in the selected language for that region.
3. The correction action returns to registration so the language or region can be changed.
4. The continue action allows registration to proceed. If no warning appears, record the case as failed.
ev: Mismatch warning, correction path and continue path; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Empty recovery email validation

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery

2. Select Continue.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Unknown recovery email privacy response
pre: Forgot your password? is open. An unregistered valid-format email is available.

2. Select Continue.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Request a password reset and open its valid link
pre: Forgot your password? is open. QA_RESET_01 and its inbox are available.
proc:
1. Enter the QA_RESET_01 email and select Continue.
2. Open the newest password-reset email for QA_RESET_01.
3. Record the stated validity period and open the link before it expires.
exp:
1. Keycloak returns to Sign In and shows You should receive an email shortly with further instructions.
2. A password-reset email for QA_RESET_01 arrives and contains a reset link.
3. The valid link opens the Update password page for QA_RESET_01.
ev: Generic request response, reset email and Update password page; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Reset-link validity wording
pre: A reset has been requested for QA_RESET_01 and its newest reset email is available.
proc:
1. Record any validity wording in the request response.
2. Record the validity period in the reset email.
3. Compare the values when both locations state a period.
exp:
1. The request response is recorded without assuming that it states a validity period.
2. The email states its reset-link validity period.
3. Any period shown in both places is consistent.
ev: Request response and reset-email validity wording; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Reset password confirmation validation
pre: A valid reset link has opened Update password.
proc:
1. Enter different valid-format values in New password and Confirm password.
2. Attempt to submit the password update.
exp:
1. Both fields accept the values and remain masked by default.
2. The update does not complete and Keycloak shows Password confirmation doesn't match.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Sign out other devices during password reset
pre: Update password is open for QA_RESET_01, which has an active session on a second approved device.
proc:
1. Enter matching valid new-password values.
2. Select Sign out from other devices and submit the update.
3. On the second device, attempt an authenticated action.
exp:
1. Both password fields contain the same masked value.
2. The password update completes with other sessions selected for sign-out.
3. The second device requires authentication again.
ev: Successful update and second-device session result; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Reject an expired password-reset link
pre: QA_RESET_01 and its inbox are available.
proc:
1. Request a reset and record the email received time and stated validity period without opening the link.
2. After the period has expired, open the link.
3. Request another reset and confirm that a new email arrives.
exp:
1. The first reset email contains a link and its validity period is recorded.
2. The expired link cannot open a usable Update password action and shows an expired or invalid-link state.
3. A new request is accepted and a new reset email arrives.
ev: Reset-email timing, expired-link state and replacement email; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Reject reuse of a password-reset link
pre: An unused reset link for QA_RESET_01 is available.
proc:
1. Use the link to set a valid new password successfully.
2. Open the same link again.
exp:
1. The first use completes the password update.
2. The same link cannot be used again and shows an invalid, expired or already-used state.
ev: Successful first use and rejected second use; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Return from Forgot Password to Sign In
pre: Forgot your password? is open.
proc: 1. Select Back to sign in.
exp: 1. Hosted Sign In opens without requesting or changing a password, and the user remains signed out.
ev: Hosted Sign In after returning; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Reset password format validation
pre: A valid reset link has opened Update password.
proc:
1. Enter matching values shorter than 12 characters that otherwise contain a number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character.
2. Repeat with at least 12 characters while omitting, one at a time, the number, lowercase letter, uppercase letter and special character.
3. Enter matching values of at least 12 characters containing every required character type. Do not submit the valid password in this case.
exp:
1. Keycloak shows Invalid password: minimum length 12.
2. Keycloak shows the corresponding numerical digit, lower case, upper case or special character message for each omitted type.
3. No password-format message is shown for the valid-format value.
ev: Each password-format message and valid-format state; execution record.

sec: Batch 8 - Forgot Password and Login Recovery
t: Verify credentials after password reset
pre: QA_RESET_01 has completed a reset. Its new and previous passwords are recorded in controlled Test Data.
proc:
1. Sign in with the new password.
2. Sign out and return to Hosted Sign In.
3. Attempt sign-in with the previous password.
exp:
1. The new password authenticates successfully.
2. Sign-out returns the user to a signed-out state.
3. The previous password is rejected with Invalid username or password.
ev: Successful new-password sign-in and rejected previous password; execution record.

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup

pre: Tell us about you / Profile Setup is open. Protocol Test Data provides a valid date of birth for this case.

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Glucose unit follows the selected country
pre: Tell us about you / Profile Setup is open. The protocol Test Data table identifies the current Country/unit mapping and a second selectable Country that uses the other supported glucose unit.
proc:

2. Open Country and select the second Test Data country.

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Controlled initial values and no stale account data
pre: Enter Tell us about you / Profile Setup from a fresh onboarding state. Before execution, the protocol Test Data table identifies any controlled initial Country/region and Glucose unit expected for this account/build. If DI/DO does not specify an initial Date of birth or Diabetes type value, those fields are observation-only and are not pass/fail criteria.
proc:
1. Before changing any field, record the displayed Date of birth, Country, Diabetes type and Glucose unit.
2. Compare only the controlled initial Country/region and Glucose unit with the values recorded in the protocol Test Data table.
3. Confirm that no personal value from a previously used test account is pre-populated as the current user’s Date of birth, Phone number or Diabetes type.

1. Every initial value explicitly controlled by Test Data matches its approved value.
2. The initial Glucose unit is consistent with the controlled Country/region mapping.
3. No personal profile value belonging to another test account is reused as the current account’s value.
4. Fields without an approved initial-value requirement are recorded as observations only and are not failed for differing defaults.
ev: Initial Profile Setup screenshot before edits; completed Test Data comparison; execution record

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Required-field Continue gating
pre: Tell Us About You / Profile Setup is open.
proc:
1. Leave at least one required field incomplete.
2. Observe Continue.
3. Complete all required fields with valid values.
4. Observe Continue again.
exp: Continue remains disabled while required data is incomplete and becomes enabled only when all required fields contain valid data.

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Phone-number validation using controlled values
pre: Tell us about you / Profile Setup is open and every other required field is valid. The protocol Test Data table provides one phone value that violates the approved phone rule, one valid phone value, and identifies the rule being verified.
proc:
1. Tap Phone number and enter the invalid Test Data value.
2. Leave/focus out of the field or use the normal form action that causes validation, then observe Phone number and Continue.
3. Replace the value with the valid Test Data phone number.
4. Repeat the same validation action and observe Phone number and Continue.
exp:
1. The invalid Test Data phone value is rejected through the controlled validation behavior and cannot make Continue available.
2. After the valid Test Data phone number is entered, the phone validation is cleared.
3. If all other required fields are valid, Continue is available after the valid phone value.
4. No numeric length boundary is inferred beyond the approved rule recorded in Test Data.
ev: Invalid-phone validation screenshot; valid-phone recovered state with Continue; completed Test Data reference; execution record

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Submission and persistence
pre: All required Profile Setup fields contain valid test data.
proc:
1. Tap Continue to submit Profile Setup.
2. Confirm navigation to the next onboarding step.
3. Return to Profile Setup and inspect the saved values.
exp: Profile data is submitted once, the app advances to the correct next onboarding step, and saved values are retained when the profile step is revisited.

sec: Batch 10 - Tell Us About You / Profile Setup
t: Back and resume / saved lock-state restoration
pre: Profile Setup has been submitted and the user has advanced to the Low Glucose Alert onboarding step.
proc:
1. Use Back to return to Profile Setup.
2. Inspect retained values and saved-field lock states.
3. Repeat the return/re-entry once to check consistency.
exp: Back navigation returns safely without duplicate submission; saved values persist and every profile field intended to be immutable is consistently restored as locked/read-only on each return.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Platform Health introduction and optional entry point

2. On iOS, verify the Apple Health introduction shows the heading/explanatory content, illustration, Continue and Not now controls.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Optional versus mandatory behavior
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Apple Health in a controlled test state.
proc: 1. Enter Apple Health. 2. Decline/skip the optional integration if a skip control is provided. 3. Continue onboarding. 4. Return later and confirm the feature can still be configured.
exp: An optional integration can be declined without blocking unrelated onboarding/app use, while any genuinely mandatory permission is clearly identified and handled according to the approved requirement.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Platform Health authorization requests Steps and Active Energy
pre: Platform-health permission has not yet been granted. On iOS the Apple Health introduction is open; on Android use the released Google Health authorization path if implemented.

4. Leave the authorization surface open without accepting yet.

2. Only the intended health read permissions required by the app are requested.
3. The app remains in a waiting state until the user chooses the permission scope.
ev: Screenshot of native health authorization surface showing requested data types; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)

4. Return to CGMx 1 and continue onboarding.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Active-Energy-only health permission
pre: Native platform-health authorization is available.

4. Return to CGMx 1 and continue onboarding.
