2. CGMx 1 returns safely from the native health surface and onboarding can continue.
3. The app must not treat Steps as authorized when it was left disabled.
ev: Screenshot of Active Energy ON / Steps OFF authorization state and app return; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Allow both Steps and Active Energy
pre: Native platform-health authorization is available.
proc:
1. Open the native health authorization surface.
2. Enable both Steps and Active Energy.
3. Confirm/Allow access.
4. Return to CGMx 1 and continue onboarding.
exp: Both requested health-data types are authorized, the app returns safely from the native authorization surface, and onboarding continues without another immediate permission request.
ev: Screenshot showing both requested health-data types enabled; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Partial health permission is respected
pre: One of the two requested health data types is authorized and the other is denied.
proc:
1. Complete health authorization with only one requested type enabled.
2. Continue onboarding and reach a screen where platform activity data can be displayed.
3. Observe whether the app displays only data permitted by the granted scope.
4. Confirm the denied data type is not presented as available.
exp: The app respects the granted scope: permitted health activity data may be used/displayed, while the denied health data type is not shown as authorized or populated from the platform health service.
ev: Permission-scope screenshot plus activity-display screenshot where available; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Permission denial
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Apple Health in a controlled test state. Device permission state can be reset/changed through OS Settings as required.
proc: 1. Trigger the relevant permission from Apple Health. 2. Choose Deny/Don’t Allow. 3. Observe the app response and attempt to continue to the dependent feature.
exp: The denial is handled without crash. The app does not falsely show the permission as granted and provides the approved safe limitation/recovery path for the dependent feature.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Revoke platform-health access and verify app response
pre: Steps and/or Active Energy access has previously been granted.
proc:
1. Confirm permitted platform-health activity can be displayed in CGMx 1.
2. Revoke CGMx 1 health access using the platform health permission manager (iOS: Health app > Profile > Privacy > Apps > CGMx 1; Android: released Google Health permission manager).
3. Return to CGMx 1.
4. Reopen the activity/dashboard view and observe the affected platform-health data.
exp: After revocation, the app does not continue presenting revoked platform-health data as currently authorized. Glucose/CGM functionality remains available and the user can re-authorize health integration through the supported permission path.
ev: Before/after permission-state screenshots and affected activity view; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Background and resume
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Apple Health in a controlled test state. Establish the target screen/state before interrupting the app.
proc: 1. Establish the target state on Apple Health. 2. Background the app for at least 10 seconds; then foreground it. 3. Repeat by force-closing/terminating the app where the title requires termination. 4. Relaunch and return to the flow.
exp: The app resumes/relaunches without crash or duplicate operation and restores the correct safe state. Previously committed data persists; incomplete actions are not silently completed or corrupted.

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Platform Health privacy and data-use disclosure
pre: Platform-health introduction is visible before authorization.
proc:
1. Open the platform-health introduction before granting access.
2. Read the explanation of why Steps and Active Energy/activity energy are requested.
3. Verify the screen states how the health data is handled locally and that health access can be changed/revoked later.
4. Verify declining the health integration does not prevent sensor connection/onboarding from continuing.
exp: The user is told the purpose of the requested health data before permission is granted, is informed that platform-health data is handled on-device/not used as CGM data, and is not led to believe health integration is mandatory for sensor connection.
ev: Screenshot of platform-health introduction/privacy wording; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Display permitted Steps and Active Energy from the platform health service
pre: Approved real device contains controlled platform-health test data for the current day/date range. Health permission is granted for both Steps and Active Energy/activity energy.
proc:
1. Grant CGMx 1 access to both Steps and Active Energy/activity energy.
2. Ensure the platform health service contains controlled activity data for the selected dashboard date range.
3. Open the CGMx 1 activity/dashboard view that presents platform-health activity.
4. Record the displayed Steps and Active Energy values/graphs.
5. Change the dashboard date/time range to another range containing known platform-health activity data and observe the update.
exp:
1. When authorized data exists, CGMx 1 displays the permitted Steps and Active Energy/activity-energy information for the selected period.
2. Changing the dashboard range refreshes the platform-health activity for the new period.
3. If the health service has no data for the selected period, the app does not fabricate activity values or treat the absence as a CGM error.
ev: Screenshot of platform health source data and corresponding CGMx 1 activity display for each tested range; execution record

sec: Batch 11 - Platform Health Integration (Apple Health / Google Health)
t: Platform-health activity is visually separated from GlucoRx CGM data
pre: Platform-health permission is granted and the activity/dashboard view contains both CGM information and third-party platform-health activity data.
proc:
1. Open the activity/dashboard view containing CGM information and permitted platform-health activity.
2. Identify the Steps and Active Energy/activity-energy presentation.
3. Compare its labels, grouping and chart/panel placement with the GlucoRx glucose presentation.
4. Confirm the third-party activity values are not presented as GlucoRx glucose measurements.
exp: Steps and Active Energy/activity-energy are displayed in clearly labelled activity content that is visually distinguishable from GlucoRx CGM glucose information. No third-party activity value can reasonably be mistaken for a glucose measurement from the CGM.
ev: Screenshot showing third-party activity presentation and GlucoRx CGM presentation on the same/related view; execution record

t: Bluetooth introduction
pre: Approved real device is in onboarding at the Bluetooth/Nearby Devices step with Bluetooth permission not yet resolved.
proc:
1. Reach the Bluetooth/Nearby Devices onboarding step.
2. Inspect the app-owned heading, explanation and action control before interacting with the OS prompt.
3. Confirm the screen explains that Bluetooth is required to connect to the CGM/transmitter.
exp: The Bluetooth/Nearby Devices onboarding screen is complete and readable, explains the CGM connection purpose, and presents an action to continue to the required OS Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission path.
ev: Screenshot of complete Bluetooth/Nearby Devices introduction screen; execution record

t: First permission request
pre: Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission is reset/not granted and the app-owned Bluetooth onboarding screen is visible.
proc:
1. Select the app action to allow/continue Bluetooth setup once.
2. Observe the native OS Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission prompt.
3. Verify the prompt is for the Bluetooth/Nearby Devices capability needed by CGMx 1.
4. Leave the prompt unanswered for evidence capture.
exp: A single native Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission prompt is shown for the intended capability; the app does not continue into CGM scanning/connection until the permission decision is resolved.
ev: Screenshot of native Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission prompt; execution record

t: Permission purpose copy
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission in a controlled test state. Device permission state can be reset/changed through OS Settings as required.
proc: 1. Open Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission. 2. Read the text relevant to “Permission purpose copy”. 3. Compare the wording with the controlled DI/DO/IFU/content reference. 4. Confirm the text is visible before the user performs the associated action.
exp: Required information and warnings match the controlled source in meaning and are presented at the correct point in the workflow. No contradictory, obsolete or misleading instruction is shown.

t: Permission allowed
pre: Native Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission prompt can be shown.
proc:
1. From the native Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission prompt, select Allow/Grant.
2. Return to CGMx 1 if the OS prompt overlays the app.
3. Continue to the next onboarding step.
4. Where a permission summary is available, verify Bluetooth is reported as Allowed/available.
exp: CGMx 1 recognizes the granted permission without repeatedly requesting it and can continue the CGM setup flow. The permission summary/status reflects Bluetooth as available.
ev: Screenshot of granted permission state and subsequent onboarding/summary state; execution record

t: Permission denied
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission in a controlled test state. Device permission state can be reset/changed through OS Settings as required.
proc: 1. Trigger the relevant permission from Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission. 2. Choose Deny/Don’t Allow. 3. Observe the app response and attempt to continue to the dependent feature.
exp: The denial is handled without crash. The app does not falsely show the permission as granted and provides the approved safe limitation/recovery path for the dependent feature.

t: Permanent denial
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device. Bluetooth hardware is ON. Bluetooth/Nearby Devices permission for CGMx 1 has already been denied. User can navigate to the Allow Bluetooth onboarding screen.
proc: 1. Open the Allow Bluetooth onboarding screen. 2. Tap Allow. 3. Observe the response when the app requests Bluetooth permission again. 4. If the native OS permission prompt does not appear, observe whether the app provides a Settings/recovery path. 5. Capture the resulting state.
exp: The app handles the already-denied permission state without crash or blank screen and does not falsely report Bluetooth permission as granted. If the OS no longer presents the normal permission prompt, the app provides the approved safe recovery path to OS Settings.

t: Open Settings recovery
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission in a controlled test state.
proc: 1. Put the relevant permission into a denied state that requires OS Settings for recovery. 2. Use the app’s Settings/recovery control. 3. Grant the permission in OS Settings. 4. Return to the app.
exp: The app opens the correct OS Settings location, refreshes the permission state on return, and enables the dependent workflow without requiring an app restart unless explicitly specified.
ev: screenshots, execution record; iOS Settings-recovery evidence includes the post-Settings onboarding restart and final permission checklist showing Bluetooth Allowed; this recovery outcome supports PASS.

t: Bluetooth hardware off
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission in a controlled test state. Test transmitter is available and Bluetooth can be toggled from device settings/quick controls.
proc: 1. Turn Bluetooth OFF at the device level. 2. Enter/return to Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission. 3. Attempt the Bluetooth-dependent action. 4. Turn Bluetooth ON and retry.
exp: The app identifies that Bluetooth is unavailable, blocks or safely pauses the dependent action with recovery guidance, and proceeds normally after Bluetooth is enabled.

t: Permission revocation
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build, OS, device and test-kit/transmitter identifiers. Reach Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission in a controlled test state. Device permission state can be reset/changed through OS Settings as required.
proc: 1. Start with the relevant permission granted and verify the dependent feature is available. 2. Revoke the permission in OS Settings. 3. Return to Bluetooth / Nearby Devices Permission and attempt the dependent action.
exp: The app detects the revoked permission, no longer presents the capability as available, and provides the approved recovery path without using the revoked permission.

t: Notification introduction
pre: Approved real device is at the notification-permission onboarding step before the native OS prompt is answered.
proc:
1. Reach the app-owned notification-permission onboarding screen.
2. Inspect the heading, explanation and Allow/continue action.
3. Verify the explanation identifies notifications/alerts as the reason for the permission request.
exp: The app-owned notification introduction is readable and explains why notification permission is needed before the native OS prompt is requested.
ev: Screenshot of app-owned notification introduction; execution record

t: First permission request
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; record app build and OS. Notification permission is reset/not yet decided. Reach Notification Permission during onboarding. Direct requirement: DO-769 / DI-760.
proc: 1. From the app-owned Notification Permission screen, trigger the notification permission action once. 2. Observe the native OS permission prompt without selecting a decision. 3. Confirm the app does not bypass the unresolved native permission decision or launch a duplicate request.
exp: The native notification permission request opens once for the intended app/capability. Until the OS decision is resolved, the app remains in the controlled permission-request state and does not falsely show notification permission as granted.

t: Permission allowed
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; native notification permission prompt is visible. Direct requirement: DO-769 / DI-760.
proc: 1. Select Allow/Grant in the native notification prompt. 2. Observe the immediate app state. 3. Confirm the granted notification state is recognized and the app proceeds only to the correct platform-specific next onboarding state without re-requesting the already-granted permission.
exp: The granted OS permission is recognized. The native prompt closes, no false denied state or duplicate request appears, and onboarding continues to the correct platform-specific next state. Notification-dependent behavior may now be enabled subject to later alert-specific permissions/settings.

t: Permission denied
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; notification permission is reset so the native request can be shown. Reach Notification Permission during onboarding. Direct requirement: DO-769 / DI-760.
proc: 1. Trigger the native notification permission request. 2. Select Deny/Don’t Allow. 3. Observe the resulting app state and attempt the available continuation/recovery action once.
exp: Denial is handled without crash or false granted status. The app remains in an explicit denied/recovery state consistent with DO-769 and does not deliver notification-dependent behavior as though permission were accepted.

t: Repeated notification denial and OS Settings recovery
pre: Notification permission has already been denied once. The platform no longer guarantees that the native prompt will be shown again.
proc:
1. Return to the app notification-permission/recovery state after a prior denial.
2. Select the action to enable notifications again.
3. If the OS no longer shows the native permission prompt, verify the app provides a route to the application notification settings.
4. Enable notifications in OS Settings.
5. Return to CGMx 1 and verify the recovery warning/status clears.
exp: After a repeated denial, the user has an actionable route to restore notification permission through the operating system. Once permission is enabled, CGMx 1 recognizes the new state and stops presenting the permission as unresolved.
ev: Screenshots of denied state, Settings recovery route, notifications enabled, and cleared app recovery state; execution record

t: OS notification categories / grouping
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; notification permission granted. Test conditions are available to generate the controlled notification priorities supported on the platform. Direct requirement: DO-770 / DI-761. DND-bypass behavior is executed in Batch 14.
proc: 1. Open the OS notification settings for CGMx 1 and identify the notification categories/channels exposed for user control. 2. Generate controlled notifications for the applicable low-priority, medium-priority and critical-alarm categories using the approved test workflow. 3. Inspect the resulting OS category/channel assignment and grouping/threading. 4. Record platform-specific category availability; execute DND-bypass behavior under Batch 14.
exp: The required OS-level notification categories/channels are identifiable and notifications are assigned/grouped according to the controlled platform design. For iOS, low-priority, medium-priority and critical-alarm categories use the controlled category/thread structure. Platform-specific differences are recorded without inventing unsupported Android category names. DND bypass is not duplicated here.

t: Foreground notification behavior
req: DI-757 / DO-871 and notification permission enabled
pre: An active CGM session and controlled live Low or High reading are available.
proc:
1. Keep CGMx 1 in the foreground on Home.
2. Cause/receive one controlled live reading that meets the configured non-critical Low or High notification condition.
3. Observe the app and system notification presentation.
4. Record the reading value, configured threshold and notification received.
exp: An eligible live threshold event is processed while the app is foregrounded without duplicate or unrelated notification behavior. The notification corresponds to the current live Low/High condition and configured threshold.
ev: Home/current-reading screenshot plus notification evidence and recorded threshold/value; execution record

t: Background notification behavior
req: DI-757 / DO-871 and notification permission enabled
pre: An active CGM session and controlled live non-critical Low or High reading are available.
proc:
1. Put CGMx 1 in the background.
2. Cause/receive one controlled live reading that meets the configured non-critical Low or High notification condition.
3. Observe the phone notification surface without first reopening the app.
4. Open CGMx 1 after capturing notification evidence.
exp: An eligible live non-critical Low/High event produces a system notification while CGMx 1 is backgrounded. Reopening the app does not duplicate the same event merely because the app returned to foreground.
ev: Background/system notification screenshot plus corresponding app reading/state; execution record

t: Revocation detected after restart
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device; notification permission is granted and onboarding has progressed/completed sufficiently to reach the normal app state. Direct requirement: DO-769 / DI-760.
proc: 1. Verify notification permission is currently granted. 2. Revoke notification permission in OS Settings. 3. Fully terminate CGMx 1 and relaunch it. 4. Observe startup and the permission recovery state without resolving it yet.
exp: On restart, CGMx 1 detects that previously granted notification permission has been lost and re-requests/requires recovery using persistent state-based UI. The app does not continue as though permission remained granted. The recovery state remains until resolved, subject to higher-priority alarm presentation.

t: Persistent notification-permission recovery clears after permission is restored
pre: Notification permission is OFF/denied and Home displays the notification recovery warning/card.
proc:
1. Capture Home with the persistent notification-permission recovery warning while permission is OFF.
2. Use the recovery action to open the supported permission route.
3. Enable notifications in OS Settings.
4. Return to CGMx 1.
5. Reopen/refresh Home if required and verify the recovery warning no longer indicates notifications are off.
exp: The recovery UI persists while notification permission is unavailable and clears only after CGMx 1 detects that permission has been restored. Current CGM readings are not blocked by the recovery warning.
ev: Before/after Home recovery screenshots and OS notification-permission state; execution record

t: Home-screen recovery after notification permission skipped
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device. Notification permission has not been granted. User can complete onboarding, connect the sensor and reach Home.
proc: 1. During onboarding, select Not now/Skip on the app-owned notification step without granting notification permission. 2. Complete onboarding and connect the sensor. 3. Reach Home and wait until a new/current glucose reading is received. 4. Confirm the Notifications are off recovery card remains visible. 5. With notification permission still OFF, produce a controlled High/Low reading and confirm no phone notification is delivered. 6. Use the Home recovery action, grant/restore notification permission, return to CGMx 1, and confirm the warning clears. 7. Produce another controlled High/Low reading and verify notification delivery.
exp: While permission is skipped/not granted, Home continues receiving current glucose readings but shows a persistent notification-recovery warning and no phone notification is delivered. After permission is restored, the warning clears and subsequent eligible alerts are delivered normally.

t: Home-screen recovery after notification permission denied
pre: Approved real iOS/Android device. Notification permission is initially undecided and the native OS permission prompt can be shown.
proc: 1. During onboarding, tap Allow and then explicitly select Don’t Allow/Don’t allow on the native OS notification prompt. 2. Complete onboarding, connect the sensor and reach Home. 3. Wait until a new/current glucose reading is received and confirm the Notifications are off recovery card is displayed. 4. With permission still denied, produce a controlled High/Low reading and confirm no phone notification is delivered. 5. Use the Home recovery action to restore notification permission in the native prompt/OS Settings. 6. Return to CGMx 1 and confirm the warning clears. 7. Produce another controlled High/Low reading and verify notification delivery.
exp: The denied permission is detected on Home, current glucose readings continue, and the app does not falsely deliver phone notifications while permission is denied. The Home recovery path restores permission, clears the warning and allows subsequent eligible notifications to be delivered.

t: Phone battery-low notification
pre: Approved real device is in an active CGM session, notifications are enabled, and the phone battery is brought to or below the approved low-battery threshold using the controlled test method recorded in Test Data.
proc:
1. Record the phone battery percentage and the approved threshold/test condition used for this run.
2. Keep the CGM session active and background CGMx 1 if required by the platform.
3. Allow the battery condition to meet the controlled low-battery criterion.
4. Observe the system notification surface.
exp: CGMx 1 provides the phone-battery-low notification required by DO-717 so the user is warned that phone charge may be insufficient for continued monitoring. The notification clearly concerns the phone battery, not the sensor/transmitter battery.
ev: Battery percentage/state screenshot and phone-battery-low notification screenshot; execution record

t: Prolonged upload-failure warning
pre: Active account/session with data available for upload. Use an approved real-device/network condition that causes uploads to continue failing for the controlled extended period without changing backend data.
proc: 1. Establish normal upload behavior. 2. Create the approved prolonged upload-failure condition. 3. Keep using the app normally until the requirement condition is reached. 4. Observe notifications. 5. Restore connectivity and observe recovery.
exp: After uploads have continually failed for the controlled extended period, the app notifies the user that data backup/upload is failing. After connectivity/service recovers, normal upload can resume without duplicate or corrupted user data.

t: Server new-data check failure notification
pre: Signed-in app with normal server synchronization available. Use an approved network/service-unavailable condition on the real device without manipulating backend records.
proc: 1. Confirm normal server data checks. 2. Establish the approved extended server-check failure condition. 3. Continue normal app use until the controlled requirement condition is reached. 4. Observe the user notification. 5. Restore service and retry.
exp: If the silent server new-data check fails for the controlled extended period, the user is notified. The app remains usable and resumes normal server checking after service is restored.

t: Notification deep link opens the appropriate feature
pre: A supported CGMx 1 low/medium-priority system notification with a defined destination has been received and is visible in the system notification surface.
proc:
1. Record the notification type and the feature/screen it is expected to open according to the controlled notification mapping.
2. With CGMx 1 backgrounded or closed as permitted, tap the notification once.
3. Observe the first app screen/feature shown after the app opens.
4. Repeat with another supported notification type where test data is available.
exp: Tapping a supported notification opens CGMx 1 and navigates to the feature mapped to that notification type. The tap does not open an unrelated screen, duplicate navigation stack, or blank state.
ev: System notification screenshot and first destination screen after tap; execution record

t: Notification history displays existing and newly received notifications
pre: Notification-history/list feature is available; at least one historical notification exists and notification delivery is enabled.
proc: 1. Open the in-app notification-history/list. 2. Record existing entries. 3. While the list is open, receive another approved notification. 4. Observe the list without leaving it. 5. Re-open the list if needed.
exp: The notification list contains historical notifications and updates to include new notifications, including a notification received while the list is being viewed. Existing history is not unexpectedly removed or duplicated.

t: Low-priority notification presentation
pre: An approved condition that generates a low-priority notification is available. System notification permission is enabled and device sound/vibration settings permit normal notifications.
proc: 1. Trigger the approved low-priority condition through normal real-device use. 2. Observe the notification banner/tray presentation. 3. Observe sound and vibration behavior.
exp: The low-priority notification is presented in normal application-notification style, uses a heads-up presentation where the OS permits, and follows the normal phone notification sound and vibration behavior.

t: Rapidly rising trend notification and nuisance-repeat prevention
pre: Notification permission is enabled and controlled real-time measurements can produce a rapidly rising trend, followed by a non-rapidly-rising/no-data transition and then another rapidly rising trend.
proc:
1. Establish a real-time rapidly rising trend and capture the first low-priority rapidly-rising notification.
2. Continue receiving rapidly rising real-time readings and verify the notification is not re-posted for every new measurement.
3. Establish a non-rapidly-rising trend or the no-data condition required by DO-953 to reset the nuisance-suppression state.
4. Re-establish a rapidly rising trend and observe notification delivery again.
exp: A rapidly rising real-time trend generates the required low-priority notification. Continued readings in the same rapidly rising state do not re-post the notification every measurement. After the reset condition defined by DO-953 occurs, a later rapidly rising trend can notify again.
ev: Trend-state/reading evidence plus first, suppressed-repeat observation and later notification evidence; execution record

t: Optional app-update notification during active session
pre: An active CGM session is running on an approved build for which an approved optional/encouraged update can be detected through the normal update mechanism.
proc: 1. Keep the CGM session active and the app operating normally. 2. Make the approved optional update available through the controlled distribution/update path. 3. Allow the app update check to occur. 4. Observe system/app notifications and session continuity.
exp: The user is notified promptly with the required low-priority update notification while the active session continues. Keep-alive/session monitoring is not intentionally interrupted merely to permit optional update installation.

t: Critical Alerts / DND onboarding screens and controls
pre: Approved real device is in onboarding at the Critical Alerts / DND configuration segment.
proc:
1. Open the Critical Alerts / DND onboarding segment.
2. Inspect each app-owned page shown before entering OS settings/permission surfaces.
3. Verify the guidance identifies the phone settings needed for critical alarm operation, including notification/critical-alert or DND/Focus requirements applicable to the platform.
4. Record the available continue/settings actions.
exp: The onboarding guidance clearly identifies the platform settings that must remain correctly configured for critical alarms and provides the applicable action(s) to resolve them. Platform-specific controls may differ, but the required critical-alarm setup meaning is present.
ev: Screenshots of Critical Alerts/DND onboarding guidance and controls; execution record

t: Permission request and grant recognition
req: DI-372 / DO-715 and notification/DND permission requirement
pre: Relevant critical-alert or DND special access is not yet granted on the test platform.
proc:
1. From the Critical Alerts/DND onboarding step, select the action that requests the platform-required permission/special access.
2. Grant the requested access in the native OS surface.
3. Return to CGMx 1.
4. Verify the corresponding onboarding/summary status changes to the granted/resolved state.
exp: The correct platform permission/special-access surface is opened, the granted state is recognized after return, and CGMx 1 no longer reports that prerequisite as unresolved.
ev: Native permission/special-access screenshot and returned granted status; execution record

t: Permission denial, revocation and recovery
pre: Relevant Critical Alerts / DND permission was previously granted. Approved real iOS and Android devices.
proc: 1. Deny or revoke the applicable permission/access in OS Settings. 2. Fully close and relaunch CGMx 1. 3. Observe Home and the permission/checklist state. 4. Use the recovery action. 5. Restore permission/access and return to the app.
exp: Loss of permission/access is detected after restart. The app does not falsely show the permission as Allowed. A persistent, actionable recovery path is provided until resolved, and restoring the permission clears the recovery state.

t: Permission state refresh after OS Settings / relaunch
pre: Relevant permission/access can be changed in OS Settings on an approved real device.
proc: 1. Change the applicable permission/access OFF in OS Settings and return/relaunch. 2. Record the app state. 3. Change it ON and return/relaunch. 4. Record the app state again.
exp: The app reflects the current OS permission/access state after return or relaunch, with no stale Allowed/Denied value or unnecessary repeated prompt.

t: iOS Critical Alerts permission and DND guidance separation
pre: iOS device. Reach the Critical Alerts permission step and the following DND guidance step.
proc: 1. Complete or skip the iOS Critical Alerts permission step. 2. Continue to the DND guidance step. 3. Inspect the action and destination offered by the DND guidance.
exp: Critical Alerts is treated as the iOS critical-notification permission. Any separate DND guidance is accurate, actionable and does not misleadingly imply an Android-style per-app DND special-access permission exists on iOS.
ev: screenshots; execution record; Quality/RA/CTO clarification if needed

t: Severe Low critical alarm presentation and acknowledgement
pre: Approved real iOS and Android devices; active CGM session; required alert permissions enabled; test kit available.
proc: 1. Generate an approved Severe Low condition. 2. Observe the OS notification and in-app alarm. 3. Confirm the displayed value/state. 4. Acknowledge or snooze using the deliberate alarm control.
exp: The Severe Low condition is surfaced as a critical alarm with prominent in-app/OS presentation and audible alarming. Deliberate acknowledgement/snooze is required and returns the alarm to the defined acknowledged/snoozed state.

t: Severe Low critical alarm bypasses Silent Mode
pre: Approved real device; required critical-alarm permission enabled. Silent/Mute mode available on the platform.
proc: 1. Turn DND/Focus OFF to isolate Silent/Mute behavior. 2. Enable Silent/Mute mode. 3. Background/lock the device. 4. Generate Severe Low. 5. Observe visual and audible alarm behavior.
exp: Where the OS permits critical-alarm bypass, the Severe Low alarm remains visibly presented and audible despite Silent/Mute mode.
ev: screenshots; execution record; tester audible confirmation

t: Severe Low critical alarm remains audible during DND / Focus
req: critical-alarm DND bypass control and DI-851 / DO-910
pre: Critical-alarm prerequisites are enabled. Put the phone in DND/Focus using the platform setting approved for this test and record the state before triggering the alarm.
proc:
1. Enable DND/Focus on the phone and confirm it is active.
2. Keep CGMx 1 backgrounded or the phone locked as applicable.
3. Receive a controlled live glucose reading at/below the fixed Critical Low threshold.
4. Observe the critical alarm sound, vibration and full-screen/urgent presentation.
5. Acknowledge/snooze the alarm using the app control.
exp: The Severe Low critical alarm is delivered with critical urgency and remains audible/vibratory through DND/Focus where the configured platform permission permits bypass. The alarm is not silently suppressed by DND/Focus.
ev: DND/Focus active screenshot plus critical-alarm presentation/acknowledgement evidence; execution record

t: Critical alarm persists and repeats until deliberate acknowledgement
pre: Approved real iOS and Android devices; Severe Low can be generated using the test kit.
proc: 1. Generate Severe Low and do not acknowledge immediately. 2. Observe persistence/repeat behavior. 3. Acknowledge/snooze deliberately. 4. Observe subsequent non-critical readings.
exp: The active critical alarm persists/repeats until deliberate acknowledgement/snooze. After acknowledgement, pending/delivered repeats for that alarm episode stop and later non-critical readings are not presented as new Critical Low events.
ev: screenshots; execution record; notification sequence evidence

t: Rapidly Falling Trend medium-priority notification
pre: Approved real iOS and Android devices; active CGM session where required; notifications enabled. Use approved real-device/test-kit conditions only. For DND-bypass verification, enable Do Not Disturb/Focus and keep the app outside any allow-list/exception that would invalidate the check. Sufficient consecutive valid readings are available to establish a real-time trend if the feature is implemented.
proc: 1. Establish a valid real-time trend window. 2. Using the approved test kit/real-device flow, attempt to create a rapidly falling trend. 3. Observe the app and OS notification behavior. 4. With DND/Focus enabled, verify whether the same medium-priority notification is presented and audible where the OS permits.
exp: A rapidly falling real-time trend generates an immediate medium-priority notification. The medium alert remains applicable until the trend changes or the no-data alarm takes over, and it bypasses DND/Focus where the OS permits.
ev: execution record; platform behavior observation; screenshots/recording where available

t: No-Data / Disconnection medium-priority alert
pre: Approved real iOS and Android devices; active CGM session where required; notifications enabled. Use approved real-device/test-kit conditions only. For DND-bypass verification, enable Do Not Disturb/Focus and keep the app outside any allow-list/exception that would invalidate the check. Active CGM session is receiving measurements before the controlled interruption.
proc: 1. Confirm current measurements are being received. 2. Create an approved controlled interruption without ending the CGM session. 3. Observe the first no-data/disconnection alarm stage before any critical escalation. 4. With DND/Focus enabled, verify whether the medium-stage alert is presented and audible. 5. Restore the normal measurement path after evidence is captured.
exp: Loss of recent measurements initiates the defined medium-priority no-data/disconnection alert before any critical escalation. The medium alert is presented with the required notification behavior, repeats as defined while unresolved, and bypasses DND/Focus where the OS permits.
ev: execution record; platform behavior observation; screenshots/recording where available

t: Incomplete trend-data medium-priority notification
req: trend-data completeness safety requirement and medium-priority notification behavior
pre: An active session can be placed in a controlled state where the latest real-time reading is present but one or more measurements required for the recent trend calculation are missing.
proc:
1. Establish the controlled incomplete-recent-trend-data condition without removing the latest real-time reading.
2. Observe the trend arrow/state on Home.
3. Observe the system notification surface for the required medium-priority warning.
4. Restore complete recent trend data and observe whether the warning condition clears/ceases.
exp: When recent data is insufficient for a valid trend calculation, the app does not show a misleading valid trend arrow and provides the required medium-priority warning. After sufficient trend data is restored, the warning condition does not continue as if data were still incomplete.
ev: Home trend-state evidence, medium-priority notification evidence, and recovery state; execution record

t: No-data alarm escalates from medium to critical priority
pre: An expected CGM session is active. Use an approved real-device condition that prevents valid measurements from arriving while the session remains expected.
proc: 1. Establish normal measurement delivery. 2. Create the approved no-data/disconnection condition. 3. Observe the initial no-data alarm. 4. Maintain the condition through the controlled escalation point. 5. Observe the escalated alarm and recover the connection.
exp: The no-data/disconnection condition first produces the required medium-priority notification and escalates to critical priority according to the controlled requirement while the expected session remains without valid data. Recovery stops further no-data escalation when measurements resume.

t: No-data escalation avoids repeated nuisance alarms during OS sleep
pre: Expected CGM session is active and the approved no-data condition can be maintained while the phone enters its normal OS sleep/doze state.
proc: 1. Establish the approved no-data/disconnection condition. 2. Allow the device to enter the normal supported sleep/doze state. 3. Maintain the condition across the controlled escalation period. 4. Wake/unlock the phone and review alarm/notification behavior.
exp: The escalation mechanism does not generate repeated nuisance critical alarms solely because the operating system slept or delayed background execution. The required no-data alarm state remains coherent and recoverable.

t: No-data alarms remain valid with incorrect phone time and while offline
pre: Expected CGM session is active. Approved test procedure permits changing untrusted phone time and disabling internet without altering backend data.
proc: 1. Establish a no-data/disconnection condition. 2. Change the device clock by the approved amount and disable internet. 3. Observe medium/critical no-data alarm behavior. 4. Restore correct time/connectivity and recover the session.
exp: No-data/disconnection alarm behavior remains functional and does not become suppressed, indefinitely delayed or spuriously cleared solely because the untrusted phone time is incorrect or the phone is offline.

t: Android Direct Boot no-data alarm after phone restart
pre: Android approved real device supports the required Direct Boot execution condition; an active CGM/no-data alarm context exists before restart. This case is Android-specific.
proc:
1. With the required CGM context established, restart the Android phone.
2. Do not unlock the phone after boot.
3. Maintain the controlled condition that should produce the no-data alarm.
4. Observe whether the Direct-Boot-capable no-data alarm/notification is delivered before first unlock.
5. Unlock the phone and verify CGMx 1 returns to a consistent alarm/session state.
exp: On Android, the required no-data alarm behavior remains available in the Direct Boot period defined by DO-923 and the state remains consistent after first unlock. This case is NR on iOS.
ev: Android restart/locked-state evidence, alarm/notification evidence before unlock, and post-unlock app state; execution record

t: Multiple simultaneous alarms preserve priority and do not suppress each other
pre: Controlled test data can make two applicable alarms/notifications active at the same time or overlap in time.
proc:
1. Record the two alarm/notification conditions to be overlapped and their priority levels.
2. Establish the first condition and confirm its presentation.
3. While it remains active, establish the second condition.
4. Observe both alarm/notification states and their priority handling.
5. Acknowledge/clear the higher-priority condition as permitted and confirm the remaining valid condition is still represented.
exp: Concurrent alarms/notifications do not incorrectly suppress or overwrite one another. Priority is preserved, and clearing one condition does not silently clear another condition that remains valid.
ev: Evidence of first condition, overlapping second condition, priority presentation and post-acknowledgement state; execution record

t: Alarm behavior remains correct with permitted future timestamp drift
pre: Approved transmitter/test data can deliver live measurements whose timestamps are drifted slightly into the permitted future range while measurements continue arriving in real time.
proc: 1. Establish normal live readings. 2. Apply/use the approved drifted-timestamp test condition. 3. Reach a threshold/trend condition that should generate an alarm/notification. 4. Observe whether the alert occurs and which reading drives it.
exp: Notifications and alarms continue to use the latest arriving real-time measurement and are not suppressed or driven by an older packet solely because the latest transmitter timestamp is slightly in the future.

t: Medium-priority notification sound, vibration, DND handling and repeat
pre: An approved medium-priority alarm condition is available; notification permission is enabled. Device DND/silent configuration is set according to the supported OS path.
proc: 1. Trigger the approved medium-priority condition. 2. Observe heads-up presentation, vibration and medium-strength sound. 3. Verify DND/silent handling where the OS supports bypass. 4. Do not acknowledge; maintain the condition through the controlled repeat interval. 5. Clear the triggering condition.
exp: The medium-priority notification uses the required heads-up presentation, vibration and medium-strength sound, bypasses DND/silent only where supported/configured, requires no acknowledgement, and repeats at the controlled interval while the triggering condition persists.

t: Critical alarm UI appears over lock screen where permitted
pre: Approved critical-low alarm test condition is available. Device is locked before the alarm is generated.
proc: 1. Lock the phone. 2. Generate the approved critical-low alarm condition. 3. Observe the display without manually unlocking first. 4. Acknowledge/recover using the approved alarm flow.
exp: While the critical-low alarm UI is active, it appears over/bypasses the lock screen where the operating system permits. The alarm is not hidden behind an ordinary locked screen when lock-screen bypass is supported.
